name: ACL Reconstruction Rehabilitation
summary: Criterion-based rehabilitation restores extension, quadriceps strength, movement quality, running and sport capacity while respecting surgical and graft-specific precautions.

looksLike: Confirm graft type, associated meniscal/cartilage procedures, surgeon restrictions and current rehabilitation phase before progressing loading
Track effusion, wound status when relevant, knee extension and flexion, pain and gait
Assess quadriceps activation and strength; document the method and compare over time
Monitor calf symptoms and screen for DVT when clinically indicated
Introduce running, hop and change-of-direction testing only when prerequisites are met and the protocol permits
redFlags: Possible DVT: new calf swelling/pain, warmth or unexplained shortness of breath; urgent medical assessment is required, with emergency response for chest pain or breathing difficulty
Possible infection: fever, increasing wound redness, drainage or rapidly worsening pain/swelling
Locked knee, sudden major extension loss or acute instability event
New neurovascular symptoms or rapid unexpected deterioration
firstSteps: Review operative note, graft and restrictions.
Check wound, effusion, extension, flexion, quadriceps activation, gait and DVT warning signs.
Start extension restoration and quadriceps activation immediately if permitted.

Assess confidence, fear of reinjury and patient-specific work/sport demands alongside physical capacity

stages.label: Treat: build capacity
stages.goal: Early priorities are extension, swelling control, quadriceps activation and normal gait.
do: Early quadriceps activation and restoration of full extension within the surgeon's protocol; avoid forcing a painful or blocked knee
Progressive closed- and open-chain strengthening according to graft, associated procedures, irritability and protocol
Hip and calf strengthening with gait retraining as needed
Balance and single-leg control, progressing only when alignment and symptom response are acceptable
Begin running only after appropriate clinical criteria and surgical restrictions are met; use a graded walk-jog progression
Add plyometrics, acceleration/deceleration and cutting in stages after adequate strength, landing control and tolerance are demonstrated
dose: Quad sets: 5–10-second holds × 10–20 reps, multiple times/day early.
Straight-leg raise when no extension lag: 2–3 sets × 8–15 reps.
Sit-to-stand/squat/leg press as allowed: 3 sets × 8–15 reps.
Progressive knee extension and hamstring work according to graft/protocol.
Later running, plyometrics and change-of-direction are criterion-based.
moveOn: Use criteria for running, jumping and return-to-sport rather than time alone
Target high quadriceps strength symmetry and quality movement
Review effusion, ROM, quadriceps capacity, movement quality and response to the previous loading stage before progressing

stages.label: Progress and self-manage
stages.goal: Later priorities are strength symmetry, landing control, running, cutting and psychological readiness.
when: Use criteria for running, jumping and return-to-sport rather than time alone
Target high quadriceps strength symmetry and quality movement
dose: Do not progress high-impact work with significant effusion or poor strength control.
Use objective strength and hop testing before return-to-sport decisions.
Aim for high limb symmetry plus good movement quality, not symmetry alone.

logic: Follow surgeon-specific restrictions first, then use criteria rather than calendar time alone for progression.
Early priorities are extension, swelling control, quadriceps activation and normal gait.
Later priorities are strength symmetry, landing control, running, cutting and psychological readiness.
manual: Patellar mobilization after surgery when safe and needed for mobility.
Gentle tibiofemoral mobilization for ROM when cleared.
Scar mobilization only after full wound healing.
modalities: NMES may assist quadriceps activation early when indicated
NMES can be paired with quadriceps contraction when activation is poor.
progression: Use criteria for running, jumping and return-to-sport rather than time alone
Target high quadriceps strength symmetry and quality movement
Review effusion, ROM, quadriceps capacity, movement quality and response to the previous loading stage before progressing
Use a multidomain return-to-sport assessment that includes strength, hop performance, landing/cutting mechanics, psychological readiness and sport-specific workload tolerance
Do not treat limb-symmetry percentages or a single hop test as sufficient clearance when both limbs may be deconditioned or movement quality is poor
Do not progress high-impact work with significant effusion or poor strength control.
Use objective strength and hop testing before return-to-sport decisions.
Aim for high limb symmetry plus good movement quality, not symmetry alone.
mistakes: Progressing based only on postoperative weeks.
Returning to sport without strength/hop testing.
education: Explain that swelling is a load-response signal.
Set expectations for long-term strength and sport-specific rehabilitation.
escalation: Contact surgical team for increasing effusion, extension block, instability, infection or DVT concern
